guard: a committed-then-lost-ack re-registration spec-write completes the same freeze instead of exiting 1 with a new frozen coordinate
why: The field loop is: spec update commits, ack is lost, the manager leaves the gate frozen and exits 1.
Boot self-heal abort-reopens, the next start freezes a NEW coordinate, and takeover never converges.
The named cell drives registerServiceInstance against an isolated KV that stores the successor spec
then throws. CONTROL: the same first registration without the lost ack still completes.
This suite imports core through ../src/index.js, so the mutation is visible without a dist rebuild.

mutations.name: PHASE 3 lost-ack always throws instead of reading the committed spec back
mutations.find: newRev = await recoverCommittedSpecWrite(kv, key, spec, current, err);
mutations.expectRed: an AMBIGUOUS first spec-write (committed then ack lost) read-back completes the same freeze rather than leaving a stuck gate
mutations.cell: an AMBIGUOUS first spec-write (committed then ack lost) read-back completes the same freeze rather than leaving a stuck gate
mutations.note: The earliest cell that uses recoverCommittedSpecWrite. The later #1243 re-registration cell is the same catch on an UPDATE.
